title: Supreme Court Upholds Insurer's Repudiation of Rs 2.4 Crore Fire Claim, Sets Aside NCDRC Award
case_name: New India Assurance Company Limited v. M/s Hemkund Duplex and Board Private Limited
card_summary: The Supreme Court set aside an NCDRC order directing New India Assurance to pay Rs 2.4 crore on a fire claim. The bench found the insured had filed false declarations and manipulated its accounts, breaching the policy. It held a consumer forum cannot discard a statutory surveyor's report without identifying a specific defect in it.
card_tip: A surveyor's report under a fire policy carries weight a consumer forum cannot brush aside on sympathy alone; a specific, identified flaw in the report is needed before departing from it.
verification_notes: Confirmed across LiveLaw, Verdictum and SupremeToday.ai; all three agree on the amount, the repudiation ground (false declarations, manipulated books) and the outcome (NCDRC award set aside). One secondary summary's claim that the amount was 'ordered returned' to the insurer is not corroborated elsewhere and is omitted from the card.
